pairs.subject: data-viz
pairs.evidence: src/components/ui/format.ts:32 The one shared delta classifier hardcodes the maturity-score noise band (SCORE_NOISE_BAND=2 points) and a rising-is-good polarity, with no way to pass either per metric. So callers showing other metrics work around it at the call site: CockpitDrivePanel colours deltaHex(debtDrop) but prints signedDelta(-debtDrop), DeliveryTrendPanelFoot passes a separate toneValue to get the colour right, and DeliveryActivityMomentum applies the 2-point score band to a percentage while drawing its own ▲/▼ arrow. That is exactly the per-call-site polarity and resolution fork that metric-identity warns about.

techniques.evidence: src/components/ui/format.ts:4 The generic formatter imports the score metric's resolution band and applies it to every delta. Polarity and resolution are not inputs, so callers outside the score metric decide them locally: CockpitDrivePanel.tsx:142-143 flips the sign, DeliveryTrendPanelFoot passes toneValue, and DeliveryActivityMomentum.tsx:40-41 draws a hand-rolled arrow under a score-band hue.

src/components/ui/format.ts:16 One authority for the direction arrow, colour and label, paired with the --color-tone-* CSS tokens. A delta within the band gets ≈ and slate rather than a muted arrow, so the direction vocabulary is withheld. Caveat: colour follows sign, not favourability, which is the polarity gap recorded under metric-identity.

src/components/ui/format.ts:52 A non-finite delta (no baseline, or divide-by-zero) renders as a neutral dash, and toneFor maps it to flat. Absence is never drawn as a confident decline. Pinned in format.test.ts.
